command: npm test && git add -A && git commit -m "fix: flaky retry test"
why: git add -A sweeps every change in the tree into one blanket stage before committing.

command: git add . && git commit -m "sync working tree before rebase"
why: Stages the entire worktree root with git add ., committing whatever happens to be lying around.

command: git commit -am "fix: null check in parser"
why: The -a flag stages every modified tracked file at commit time, a whole-tree sweep.
The :/ pathspec resolves to the repository root, so this stages the whole tree.
The pathspec only excludes two directories, which still sweeps in everything else in the tree.
Command substitution expands to every modified file, staging all worktree changes at once.
Removes every tracked file from the index in one sweep.
Finds matching files across the whole tree and stages them all through xargs.
--all under git -C blanket-stages the whole repo at /work/repo.
The variable hides git add --all and eval runs it, staging everything.

command:
pytest -q tests/
git add -A
git commit -m "test: cover retry logic"
why: Ordinary test run, but the second line blanket-stages with git add -A before committing.
Python spawns git add -A, staging the whole tree from inside another language.
The piped string reaches sh as git add -A, a blanket stage.
--no-verify skips the pre-commit and commit-msg hooks.
Pushes with --no-verify, skipping the repository's pre-push hook.
Inline -c config points core.hooksPath at /dev/null so the commit runs hookless.

command: git config --unset core.hooksPath && git commit -m "chore: cleanup"
why: Unsetting core.hooksPath redirects the repo away from its configured hooks before committing.

command:
export HUSKY=0
git add src/api/
git commit -m "chore: bump deps"
why: The export line turns off husky so the commit on line three skips the hooks.

command: SKIP=pre-commit git commit -m "test: add edge case"
why: The SKIP env var tells the pre-commit framework to skip the pre-commit hook.
Deletes the pre-commit and pre-push hook files outright.
Removes the .husky directory, deleting every husky-managed hook.
Strips the executable bit from the pre-commit hook so git no longer runs it.
Moves the pre-commit hook out of .git/hooks, disarming it.

command: TREE=$(git write-tree) && COMMIT=$(git commit-tree $TREE -p HEAD -m "chore: snapshot") && git update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT
why: Builds a commit and moves the ref with plumbing, bypassing every commit hook.

command: git config alias.yolo 'commit --no-verify'; git yolo -m "fix: ship it"
why: Defines and runs a git alias whose expansion commits with --no-verify.
A hard reset throws away all uncommitted work and moves back a commit.
cd into the bugfix worktree then hard-resets to origin/main, discarding its uncommitted work.
checkout -- . discards every modified file in the worktree at once.
clean -fdx force-removes all untracked files and ignored build artifacts.
Forced checkout silently drops uncommitted changes when switching to release/1.4.
-D force-deletes a branch that may still hold unmerged work.
Force push overwrites remote history on the hotfix branch.
The +refspec spelling is a force push of main.
Deletes the remote branch feature/old-api, destroying pushed work.
A mirror push replicates and deletes remote refs wholesale.
stash clear throws away every stashed change with no way back.
Expiring all reflogs immediately destroys the safety net for unreachable commits.
Deleting .git destroys all history and uncommitted work.
--force removes the worktree even if it holds uncommitted or untracked work.

command:
cat > /tmp/ship.sh <<'EOF'
set -e
git push --force origin main
EOF
bash /tmp/ship.sh
why: The heredoc writes a script whose bash run force-pushes main.
Read-only status check.
Stages two named files only.
Interactive patch staging of a named directory.

command: git commit -m "fix: null check in parser"
why: Commits only what is already staged.
Read-only log across all refs; --all here is a log flag, not a stage sweep.
Read-only diff summary.
Soft reset moves HEAD but keeps all work staged, destroying nothing.
Unstages one named file while keeping its edits in the worktree.
Dry-run clean only prints what would be removed.
Restores a single named file, an explicitly allowed action even with unsaved edits to it.
Discards edits to one named file only, which the policy allows.
--force appears only inside the commit message text.
Stages a file literally named all.txt, not the whole tree.
Reinstalling dependencies; node_modules is ignored, not tracked work.
-d only deletes a branch that git has verified is merged.
Renaming the current branch, explicitly allowed.
Normal non-forced push of a feature branch.
--dry-run only prints what a push would do; the -n spelling on push is not --no-verify.
Garbage collection is an allowed maintenance command.
Deleting a local tag is explicitly allowed.
Stashing saves current work in a recoverable stash.
Pops the stash back into the worktree without destroying anything.

command: git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main
why: Fetch followed by a normal rebase onto a branch, which keeps work recoverable.
A normal merge of a feature branch; --no-ff only affects merge shape.
Pointing core.hooksPath at .githooks is the one allowed value.

command: git -c core.hooksPath=.githooks commit -m "fix: use repo hooks dir"
why: Inline -c config points hooks at the allowed .githooks directory for this one commit.
Normal named edit of a hook file's contents, which the policy allows.
Runs the pre-commit hook directly instead of disabling it.

command:
# never run git reset --hard during this rebase
git status --short
why: The forbidden text is only a comment; the command actually run is read-only status.
Read-only diff of the staged changes via git -C.
Stages a named directory below the root, not the whole tree.
Removes one named file from the index while keeping the working copy.
Normal branch switch carries or refuses local changes but never discards them.
Creating a worktree destroys nothing and leaves existing work untouched.
Worktree removal without --force; git itself refuses if the worktree holds uncommitted work.

command: cd /work/wt-bugfix && git add src/parser/fix.ts && git commit -m "fix: off-by-one in tokenizer"
why: Inside the worktree, stages one named file and commits only what is staged.
Defines and runs a read-only git alias.

command:
cat > /tmp/prep.sh <<'EOF'
set -e
pytest -q tests/
git add src/ tests/
git commit -m "chore: green build"
EOF
bash /tmp/prep.sh
why: The heredoc script runs tests, stages two named directories, and commits only that.

command: lint_fix() { ruff check --fix src/; }; lint_fix && git add src/
why: A helper function fixes lint then stages the named src/ directory.
Revert creates a new commit undoing HEAD, destroying nothing.
